title: Linear Algebra You Actually Need for AI

sections.subtitle: Vectors and dot products
sections.description:
A vector is a direction and a magnitude. The dot product measures how much two vectors point in the same direction.

Cosine similarity normalizes that dot product by both magnitudes, giving a score between -1 and 1.

consoleBlock.py:
import math

a = [0.9, 0.4]
b = [0.7, 0.6]

dot = sum(x * y for x, y in zip(a, b))
norm_a = math.sqrt(sum(x * x for x in a))
norm_b = math.sqrt(sum(y * y for y in b))
cosine = dot / (norm_a * norm_b)

print("dot:", round(dot, 3))
print("cosine similarity:", round(cosine, 3))

sections.subtitle: Matrices are transformations
sections.description:
A matrix-vector product transforms a vector into a new space. Every neural network layer is a matrix multiplication followed by a non-linearity.

Shape discipline prevents most bugs: an (m, n) matrix times an (n,) vector produces an (m,) vector.

consoleBlock.py:
matrix = [
    [1, 2],
    [3, 4],
]
vector = [5, 6]

result = [
    sum(row[i] * vector[i] for i in range(len(vector)))
    for row in matrix
]

print(result)
